query: If the ticket types that create the heaviest agent workload were reduced, how much would resolution time drop?

per_column.name: resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: Resolution time is the core outcome variable for this query and provides genuine analytical leverage. However, values are derived from opened_at/closed_at timestamps, and many produced values are negative (e.g. -4.2902, -106.7164), which are impossible durations and contradict a sound reading of the timestamps. This signals a computation error rather than a faithful reading of the source, lowering groundedness.

per_column.name: category_avg_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: A per-category average resolution time is a useful aggregate for comparing category burdens and modeling the counterfactual. It is derivable from the table by grouping on category and averaging resolution_hours. It inherits some noise from the flawed resolution_hours base, but as a categorisation-level aggregate it is a warranted derivation.

per_column.name: category_workload_rank
per_column.rationale: Ranking categories by workload directly serves the query's need to identify 'heaviest workload' ticket types, giving a clean axis to prioritise. The rank aligns with category frequency counts derivable from the table (284/109/72/26/9), so it is well grounded.

per_column.name: is_high_workload_category
per_column.rationale: A binary flag for the top workload category is a usable grouping key for the counterfactual, though it is largely redundant with category_workload_rank==1, reducing its independent leverage. Values are grounded, mapping directly to the highest-frequency category.

per_column.name: counterfactual_resolution_hours
per_column.rationale: This column directly operationalises the 'how much would resolution time drop' query by replacing high-workload-category values with a substitute (214.2197), which is genuinely useful. However it inherits and propagates the invalid negative resolution values, and the substitute constant is a modeling artifact rather than a value read from the source text, so groundedness is compromised.

judge.rationale: As a set the columns give real analytical leverage for the query: they quantify resolution time, aggregate and rank workload by category, and construct an explicit counterfactual answering 'how much would time drop.' The main groundedness concern is the pervasive negative resolution_hours values (impossible durations), which contradict a sound reading of the opened/closed timestamps and propagate into the counterfactual column. The rank/flag/average columns are well grounded and derivable from the table. Judged only against usefulness and groundedness (not completeness), the columns are broadly sound but flawed by the erroneous duration computation.
